segmentation.text: No person shall park
a vehicle
in an access aisle.

elements.justification: 'Park' applies DEF-NRS-484A-155: 'the standing of a vehicle, whether occupied or not, otherwise than temporarily for the purpose of and while actually engaged in loading or unloading of merchandise or passengers'. drv.motion.parked denotes 'the standing of a vehicle, whether occupied or not, observed as a at rest at every observation of the window behind the observation, of length min_duration'; 'A halt shorter than min_duration, which may be the temporary halt the definition leaves out, is not denoted', which carries the definition's exclusion of a temporary halt for loading. Same mapping as the index's 'It shall be unlawful for any person to park' (LVMC_11_40_170).

'vehicle' is admitted as the aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; ru.aggregate is 'membership of a legal aggregate'. It is not a relational role (who drives) and no class atom replaces an admitted aggregate.

'Access aisle' applies DEF-LVMC-11-02-030: an area 'Adjacent to a parking space designated for the handicapped' and 'Marked by spaced, crosshatched or diagonal stripes'. st.parking_space is a 'marked bay for standing or parking; designation in {general, disabled, disabled_side_lift, access_aisle, municipal, charging}': the designation access_aisle is the marked aisle beside a disabled bay. 'in' places the vehicle there: rel.occupies, 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region', anchors the vehicle to the aisle it is in, not to any aisle of the scene.

applicability: The subject is a vehicle (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle) and its footprint overlaps a parking-space region whose designation is access_aisle (st.parking_space, rel.occupies) at the observation.
obligation: The subject is not parked (drv.motion.parked with speed_tol p.halt_speed_tolerance and min_duration p.parking_min_duration) while its footprint overlaps that access-aisle region: for every parking-space region of designation access_aisle the subject occupies at the observation, the subject is not parked there.

narrowings.why: 'No person shall park' is read through the vehicle's own standing; whoever or whatever controls it, the duty binds the vehicle's conduct.

The definition's exclusion of a halt made 'temporarily for the purpose of and while actually engaged in loading or unloading' is read through the halt's duration: a halt shorter than p.parking_min_duration is the temporary halt and is not parking; the loading purpose itself is not observed.

The defined area's design for 'unobstructed ingress, egress and access' and its adjacency to a disabled bay are read through the mapped marking: a parking-space region the source designates access_aisle is the access aisle.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A passenger car (vehicle aggregate) comes to rest with its footprint overlapping a st.parking_space of designation access_aisle beside a disabled bay and stays at rest there (kin.speed at or below the tolerance) for longer than p.parking_min_duration.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: A passenger car halts briefly in an access-aisle parking space, shorter than p.parking_min_duration, to let a passenger out, then drives off; drv.motion.parked never holds while it occupies the aisle.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: A passenger car parks for a long time in a parking space of designation general; its footprint never overlaps an access_aisle region.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: A passenger car stands at rest next to an access-aisle region for longer than p.parking_min_duration; the source does not observe rel.occupies, so whether it is in the aisle is unknown.

segmentation.text: A vehicle
otherwise lawfully
parked in an alley
shall not park for a greater period than thirty minutes within any one-hour period.

elements.justification: 'vehicle' is admitted as DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; ru.aggregate is 'membership of a legal aggregate', never a relational role or a class list.

'parked' applies DEF-NRS-484A-155 'the standing of a vehicle, whether occupied or not, otherwise than temporarily ...', carried by drv.motion.parked ('at rest at every observation of the window behind ... of length min_duration'; a shorter halt 'is not denoted'). 'Alley' applies DEF-NRS-484A-015 'a highway ... Within a city block ... Which primarily services access to the rear entrance of abutting property'; st.alley is 'a narrow way within a block serving the rear of properties'. rel.occupies ('a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region', whose list names the alley) anchors the vehicle to the alley it is parked in.

Nearest carriers only (the span carries an operator gap): the obligation limits the total time the vehicle is parked (drv.motion.parked) in the alley (rel.occupies, st.alley) within any one-hour window behind the observation, measured on kin.time ('instant of observation of a scene'). holdsFor measures only one continuous run and Term.sinceRise only the latest run, so neither sums several parked periods within the hour; the cumulative duration is not written by any operator.

residues.why: 'otherwise lawfully' states that a vehicle whose parking complies with every other rule is still held to the thirty-minute limit; it does not exempt a vehicle parked unlawfully in another respect, which is no less held to the limit. The duty is the same whether or not the vehicle's parking otherwise complies.

applicability: The subject is a vehicle and is parked (drv.motion.parked with p.halt_speed_tolerance, p.parking_min_duration) with its footprint overlapping an alley region (st.alley, rel.occupies) at the observation.
obligation: Within the one-hour window behind the observation, the total time during which the subject was parked in that alley is not greater than thirty minutes (the literals of span s4). The cumulative duration over several parked periods is the operator gap of span s4.

narrowings.why: The definition's exclusion of a temporary halt for loading or unloading is read through the halt's duration (drv.motion.parked's min_duration); the loading purpose is not observed.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A passenger car comes to rest in an alley (rel.occupies st.alley) and stays at rest there for forty minutes.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: A passenger car parks in an alley for ten minutes and then drives out of the alley; it does not return within the hour.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: A passenger car parks for an hour on a street (st.highway) that is not an alley; its footprint never overlaps an st.alley region.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: A passenger car stands at rest for forty minutes at the mouth of an alley; the source does not observe rel.occupies, so whether it is in the alley is unknown.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: A passenger car parks in an alley for twenty minutes, drives out for five minutes, and returns to park in the same alley for another twenty minutes: forty minutes parked within one hour.

gaps.proposal: durationWithin (m : Measure) (d : Term) (subject : String) (φ : Formula) : Term -- the total time, within the window of length d behind the observation, during which φ held (each interval between consecutive observations counted where φ held at both its ends), unknown where the window is truncated or φ is unknown on a part that could change the comparison. It decides the action the law forbids: a vehicle parked in an alley for more than the stated time in total within any one-hour period, over several parked periods; holdsFor and sinceRise measure one continuous run only, so a vehicle that leaves briefly and returns escapes them.

segmentation.text: Except for a motor vehicle,
no person shall park
any vehicle
on any street
for a period of time longer than thirty minutes
between the hours of one a.m. and six a.m. of any day.

elements.justification: 'motor vehicle' is admitted as DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle ('every vehicle which is self-propelled but not operated upon rails'); ru.aggregate is 'membership of a legal aggregate'. The class atom ru.motor_vehicle never replaces an admitted aggregate.

'park' applies DEF-NRS-484A-155 'the standing of a vehicle, whether occupied or not, otherwise than temporarily for the purpose of and while actually engaged in loading or unloading'; drv.motion.parked denotes 'at rest at every observation of the window behind the observation, of length min_duration', a shorter halt 'is not denoted'. Same mapping as the index's 'It shall be unlawful for any person to park'.
'vehicle' is admitted as DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; ru.aggregate is 'membership of a legal aggregate'.

'Street' applies DEF-NRS-484A-265 'the entire width between the boundary lines of every highway inside the territorial limits of a city'; st.highway is 'the entire public way between its boundary lines, including sidewalks and shoulders' (not the roadway alone, whose exclusion does not apply since the definition takes the entire width). rel.occupies anchors the vehicle's footprint on it. Same mapping as the index's 'upon any street' (LVMC_11_48_050); the city limits are the jurisdiction this city ordinance applies in.

'for a period of time longer than thirty minutes' is one continuous period of parking, a time window behind the observation of the stated length at every observation of which the vehicle was parked on the street within the hours; the window reads kin.time, 'instant of observation of a scene'.

env.civil_time is 'the local calendar time of the observation: date, weekday, time of day (from the recording's metadata, not from the scene)'; the law states the hours itself, so the time of day is compared with the stated one a.m. and six a.m. 'Not a stand-in for: kin.time' does not apply: the clock of day, not the order of observations, is read. Same mapping as the index's 'between the hours of seven p.m. and six a.m.;' (LVMC_11_48_050).

applicability: The subject is a vehicle and not a motor vehicle (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle does not hold), its footprint overlaps a street (st.highway, rel.occupies), and the civil time of day (env.civil_time) is at or after one a.m. and before six a.m.
obligation: It is not the case that, at every observation of the time window of thirty minutes behind the observation, the subject was parked (drv.motion.parked with p.halt_speed_tolerance, p.parking_min_duration) with its footprint on a street and with the civil time of day at or after one a.m. and before six a.m.

narrowings.why: 'no person shall park' is read through the vehicle's own standing, whoever controls it; the definition's temporary halt for loading or unloading is read through the halt's duration (min_duration), the purpose itself not being observed.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: A trailer stands at rest on a street from 02:00 to 02:20 civil time and is then towed away.

scenarios.name: blind

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: A trailer stands at rest on a street from 00:30 to 01:20 civil time and is then towed away: only twenty minutes of the period lie within the hours.

segmentation.text: Except as otherwise provided in this Section
or as permitted by posted sign,
it is unlawful for a person to stand, park or store,
upon any street
adjacent to a residence district, public school or public park,
a commercial vehicle, recreational vehicle, trailer,
or any combination of vehicle and trailer
having an overall length of twenty-four feet or more
or an unladen weight in excess of eight thousand pounds.

For purposes of the preceding sentence, a "residence district" means the territory contiguous to a street, not comprising a business district, in which the parcels abutting such street for a distance of three hundred feet or more are mainly occupied by dwellings or by dwellings and buildings in use for residence.
The provisions of Subsection (A) do not apply to a commercial vehicle that is:
(1) Parked in front of property from which or to which goods or passengers are being picked up or delivered,
but only for that period of time during which goods or passengers are being expeditiously loaded or unloaded;
or (2) Being used in conjunction with the performance of service, repair, construction or similar essential use within the immediate neighborhood.

elements.justification: Nearest carriers only (atom gap): dev.regulatory_sign's codes (no_stopping, no_standing, no_parking, angle_parking, ...) prohibit or regulate and none permits the standing or parking of a vehicle class; dev.zone_sign kind parking_restricted with its conditions states where a restriction applies, and a condition that holds there makes the restriction apply rather than permitting the vehicle. None carries a posted permission.

'stand' applies DEF-NRS-484A-250 'the halting of a vehicle, whether occupied or not, otherwise than for the purpose of and while actually engaged in receiving or discharging passengers'; 'park' DEF-NRS-484A-155; 'store' is a longer standing still. Standing contains parking and storing, so the three are one prohibition of standing: drv.motion.parked ('at rest at every observation of the window behind ... of length min_duration') with the standing window p.standing_min_duration, as the index maps 'No person shall stand or park a vehicle' (LVMC_11_52_040_A).

'Street' applies DEF-NRS-484A-265 'the entire width between the boundary lines of every highway inside the territorial limits of a city'; st.highway is 'the entire public way between its boundary lines, including sidewalks and shoulders', not the roadway alone. rel.occupies anchors the vehicle on it. Same mapping as the index's 'upon any street'.

Each word is an admitted aggregate: 'commercial vehicle' DEF-LVMC-11-02-070::commercial_vehicle, 'recreational vehicle' DEF-LVMC-11-02-110::recreational_vehicle, 'trailer' DEF-LVMC-11-02-170::trailer; ru.aggregate is 'membership of a legal aggregate', never expanded into classes.

'combination of vehicle and trailer' is no defined term; ru.trailer_or_combination is 'vehicle drawn by another, or the combination', which denotes the combination as one road user. Its members are a 'vehicle' (admitted DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle) and a 'trailer' (admitted DEF-LVMC-11-02-170::trailer), each claimed as its aggregate.

kin.extent is 'the body's size along its axes about the reference point ... a formula reads the full length, width and height'; the overall length is its length, compared with the stated twenty-four feet.

Nearest carriers only (atom gap): ru.commercial_motor_vehicle is a 'vehicle over the jurisdiction's commercial mass class or marked as commercially licensed', a class threshold the jurisdiction sets, not the stated unladen weight of eight thousand pounds; kin.extent is the body's size, not its mass. No atom carries a vehicle's unladen weight.

'commercial vehicle' is admitted as DEF-LVMC-11-02-070::commercial_vehicle ('a motor vehicle or combination of motor vehicle and trailer maintained or used primarily for the furtherance of a commercial enterprise'); the exceptions (1) and (2) are read only for a subject that is one.

Goods or passengers being picked up or delivered is a purpose, read by the conduct it explains: the commercial vehicle is at rest (drv.motion.complete_halt, 'at rest at the observation ... complete cessation from movement') with a door open (sig.door_open, 'a door open; side in {traffic, curb}') through which goods or passengers pass. 'In front of property' is any frontage the street serves and restricts nothing beyond the vehicle standing on the street.

Nearest carriers only (atom gap): ru.official_vehicle is 'a vehicle in official or contracted road service', a livery class, not a vehicle's use at a nearby job ('Not a stand-in for: an emergency vehicle' aside, it does not say what the vehicle is used for now); dev.temporary_traffic_control marks 'works, a closure or an obstruction' on the road, not service, repair or construction at a property in the neighborhood. No atom carries a vehicle's present use for such work.

operationalizations.convention: the excepted period is the current halt (drv.motion.complete_halt with p.halt_speed_tolerance) measured from its onset (time since the halt last became true, on kin.time) up to p.commercial_loading_max_halt, the thirty-minute limit common to commercial loading zones: a halt longer than that is not expeditious loading

assumptions.meaning: the street the road user is on at the observation is adjacent to a residence district, to the grounds of a public school or to a public park, as the map's reading classifies the street's frontage

residues.why: The provisions of this Section that provide otherwise are its subsection (B), whose exceptions (1) and (2) are spans a11 to a14 of this same line, carried by this node; the words add no exception beyond them, so the duty is the same whether or not they are read.

The section's own meaning of 'residence district' is the classification the map's reading applies when it declares asm.street_adjacent_to_residence_school_or_park, which carries span a5; a residence district is a legal region class, so the definition is carried by that declaration and imposes no condition of its own beyond it.

applicability: The subject is a commercial vehicle, a recreational vehicle, a trailer, or a vehicle that is a vehicle-and-trailer combination (ru.trailer_or_combination); its overall length (kin.extent length) is at least twenty-four feet or its unladen weight exceeds eight thousand pounds (atom gap of span a9); its footprint is on a street (st.highway, rel.occupies); the assumption asm.street_adjacent_to_residence_school_or_park holds; no posted sign permits its standing there (atom gap of span a2); and it is not a commercial vehicle excepted by (1) — at rest with a door open in a halt that has lasted no longer than p.commercial_loading_max_halt — or by (2) — in use for nearby service, repair or construction work (atom gap of span a14).
obligation: The subject is not standing (drv.motion.parked with p.halt_speed_tolerance and min_duration p.standing_min_duration) on that street.

narrowings.why: 'it is unlawful for a person to stand, park or store' is read through the vehicle's own standing, whoever controls it; the definitions' exclusion of a halt for receiving or discharging passengers or loading is read through the halt's duration (p.standing_min_duration), the purpose not being observed.
Goods or passengers being picked up or delivered is read through the commercial vehicle at rest with a door open; the purpose itself is not observed.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A trailer (trailer aggregate) with a kin.extent length of ten metres stands at rest for ten minutes on a street for which asm.street_adjacent_to_residence_school_or_park is declared; no sign is posted.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: A recreational vehicle with a kin.extent length of ten metres drives along a street adjacent to a residence district and halts for twenty seconds at a signal, then continues; it never stands for p.standing_min_duration.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: A trailer with a kin.extent length of ten metres stands at rest for an hour on a street for which the assumption asm.street_adjacent_to_residence_school_or_park is declared false.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: A trailer ten metres long stands at rest for ten minutes beside a street adjacent to a residence district; the source does not observe rel.occupies, so whether it stands on the street is unknown.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: A commercial vehicle ten metres long stands at rest on a street adjacent to a residence district with a door open (sig.door_open) for ten minutes, then drives off: exception (1) within the expeditious-loading bound.

gaps.proposal: `dev.parking_permission_sign` | a posted sign permitting the standing, parking or storage of a vehicle class at the place it governs, with the same structured **conditions** attribute as `dev.zone_sign` (hours, days, duration, class) **Not a stand-in for:** a restriction sign (`dev.regulatory_sign` no_parking or no_standing, `dev.zone_sign` parking_restricted) — a permission excuses where a restriction forbids | general. It decides where the law permits the standing it otherwise forbids.

`ru.unladen_mass` | the mass of a vehicle without load, as registered or measured (kg); for a combination, the sum of its units **Not a stand-in for:** the body's size (`kin.extent`) or a commercial class (`ru.commercial_motor_vehicle`) | general. It decides which road users the duty concerns: a vehicle shorter than the stated length but heavier than the stated weight.

`ru.work_service_use` | the vehicle is in use for service, repair, construction or similar work at a site near where it stands, as the source records its assignment or observes its work equipment deployed or its crew at work beside it **Not a stand-in for:** a vehicle in official road service (`ru.official_vehicle`) or works on the road (`dev.temporary_traffic_control`) | general. It decides which commercial vehicles the duty excuses.

segmentation.text: The City Council may designate parking spaces upon City streets or in City parking facilities for the parking of City vehicles.
It is unlawful to park
a vehicle
other than a City vehicle
in any such space that has been duly posted or marked.

elements.justification: The designated space is the referent of 'such space' in s5. st.parking_space is a 'marked bay for standing or parking; ... designation in {general, disabled, disabled_side_lift, access_aisle, municipal, charging}': designation municipal is a bay reserved for the city's own vehicles, whether on a street or in a city parking facility (DEF-LVMC-11-02-050: a lot or garage 'which the City owns, operates or maintains'); the place of the bay restricts nothing beyond its municipal designation, which the Council makes only there.

'park' applies DEF-NRS-484A-155 'the standing of a vehicle, whether occupied or not, otherwise than temporarily for the purpose of and while actually engaged in loading or unloading'; drv.motion.parked denotes 'at rest at every observation of the window behind ... of length min_duration', a shorter halt 'is not denoted'. Same mapping as the index's 'It shall be unlawful for any person to park'.
'vehicle' is admitted as DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; ru.aggregate is 'membership of a legal aggregate'.

A City vehicle is one the incorporated city (DEF-NRS-484A-045) operates; ru.official_vehicle is 'a vehicle in official or contracted road service, identifiable by livery or equipment; kind in {..., municipal, ...}', and kind municipal is the city's own vehicle. 'Not a stand-in for: an emergency vehicle' is respected: the exception reads the municipal kind, not the emergency class.

'such space' is the space s1 designates: a st.parking_space of designation municipal; 'duly posted or marked' is its posting or marking, whose presence on the road is the evidence of the designation. rel.occupies ('a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region') anchors the vehicle in that space, not any municipal space of the scene.

applicability: The subject is a vehicle that is not a municipal official vehicle (ru.official_vehicle kind municipal does not hold), and its footprint overlaps a parking-space region of designation municipal (st.parking_space, rel.occupies) at the observation.
obligation: For every parking-space region of designation municipal the subject occupies at the observation, the subject is not parked there (drv.motion.parked with p.halt_speed_tolerance, p.parking_min_duration).

narrowings.why: That the space was designated by the City Council and 'duly posted or marked' is read through the mapped municipal designation of the bay, the posting or marking on the road being the evidence of the designation.
The definition's temporary halt for loading or unloading is read through the halt's duration (min_duration p.parking_min_duration); the loading purpose is not observed.

A City vehicle is recognized by its municipal livery or equipment (ru.official_vehicle kind municipal); a city-owned vehicle without such livery, or a city emergency vehicle the source labels only by its emergency class, is read as not a City vehicle, so the duty is applied to it.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: A private passenger car stays at rest for an hour in a parking space of designation general; it occupies no municipal space.

segmentation.text: The operator of a bus,
other than a tour bus,
shall: Not stand or park such vehicle
upon any street
at any place other than a bus stop, bus stand or the origin or destination point
for the route to which such vehicle is assigned
which has been designated in accordance with Section 11.60.010 [DEF-LVMC-11-60-010] of this Chapter.

elements.justification: 'bus' is admitted as DEF-NRS-484A-030::bus; ru.aggregate is 'membership of a legal aggregate'. 'The operator of' names who controls the bus, a relational role that is no membership: the duty binds the bus's own conduct.
'tour bus' is admitted as DEF-LVMC-11-02-150::tour_bus; ru.aggregate is 'membership of a legal aggregate'; the class atom ru.tour_bus_or_limousine never replaces an admitted aggregate.

'stand' applies DEF-NRS-484A-250 'the halting of a vehicle, whether occupied or not, otherwise than for the purpose of and while actually engaged in receiving or discharging passengers', and 'park' DEF-NRS-484A-155, a standing; standing contains parking, so the prohibition is one of standing: drv.motion.parked ('at rest at every observation of the window behind ... of length min_duration') with min_duration p.standing_min_duration, as the index maps 'No person shall stand or park a vehicle' (LVMC_11_52_040_A).

'Street' applies DEF-NRS-484A-265 'the entire width between the boundary lines of every highway inside the territorial limits of a city'; st.highway is 'the entire public way between its boundary lines', not the roadway alone. rel.occupies anchors the bus on it. Same mapping as the index's 'upon any street'.

The places are borrowed from LVMC 11.60.010, quoted in b7: 'every such bus stop, bus stand, taxicab stand, other stand or origin or destination point shall be designated by appropriate signs'. A bus stop is st.transit_stop ('a bus stop, bench, shelter or platform for public transport passengers') or st.curb_zone kind bus_stop ('a signed or marked length of curb'); a bus stand ('a fixed area in or adjacent to the highway to be occupied exclusively by buses', DEF-NRS-484A-035) and an origin or destination point, each designated by signs, are the signed bus zone, st.curb_zone kind bus_stop. rel.occupies anchors the bus at the place where it stands.

Nearest carriers only (atom gap): st.curb_zone kind bus_stop and st.transit_stop say a place serves buses, never which route's origin or destination point it is; no atom ties a bus to the route it is assigned to, or that route to its termini.

compositions.quote: every such bus stop, bus stand, taxicab stand, other stand or origin or destination point shall be designated by appropriate signs

applicability: The subject is a bus and not a tour bus, its footprint overlaps a street (st.highway, rel.occupies), and it does not occupy a bus stop (st.transit_stop, or st.curb_zone of kind bus_stop) nor a signed bus stand or the signed origin or destination point of the route it is assigned to (st.curb_zone of kind bus_stop; the route tie is the atom gap of span b6).
obligation: The subject is not standing (drv.motion.parked with p.halt_speed_tolerance and min_duration p.standing_min_duration) on that street.

narrowings.why: 'The operator of a bus' is read through the bus's own controlled motion, whoever or whatever is at the controls.
The definitions' exclusion of a halt for receiving or discharging passengers, or for loading, is read through the halt's duration (p.standing_min_duration); the purpose is not observed.

segmentation.text: The operator of a bus,
other than a tour bus,
shall: Not stop such vehicle
upon any street
at any place for the purpose of loading or unloading passengers or their baggage
other than at a bus stop, bus stand, passenger loading zone or the origin or destination point
for the route to which such vehicle is assigned
which has been designated in accordance with Section 11.60.010 [DEF-LVMC-11-60-010]
except in case of an emergency.

elements.justification: 'bus' is admitted as DEF-NRS-484A-030::bus; ru.aggregate is 'membership of a legal aggregate'; 'the operator of' is a relational role, never membership.
'tour bus' is admitted as DEF-LVMC-11-02-150::tour_bus; ru.aggregate is 'membership of a legal aggregate'.

'Stop' where prohibited is DEF-NRS-484A-260 by its own scope ('when prohibited'): 'any halting, even momentarily, of a vehicle, whether occupied or not, except when necessary to avoid conflict with other traffic or in compliance with the directions of a police officer or official traffic-control device'. The halting is drv.motion.complete_halt ('at rest at the observation'); the definition's exclusions, which that concept does not make, are carried beside it as in the index's LVMC_11_52_130_A11: a halt behind another road user ahead in the same lane within the queue gap (rel.ahead_behind_in_lane, rel.surface_gap), and a halt at a travel region the bus occupies (rel.occupies, st.travel_region) governed (dev.governs) by a traffic signal, stop sign, yield sign or railway signal or gate, or under a person's stop direction (dev.human_direction).

'Street' applies DEF-NRS-484A-265 'the entire width between the boundary lines of every highway inside the territorial limits of a city'; st.highway is 'the entire public way between its boundary lines', not the roadway alone. Same mapping as the index's 'upon any street'.

Loading or unloading passengers or their baggage is a purpose, read by the conduct it explains: the halted bus has a door open (sig.door_open, 'a door open; side in {traffic, curb}'), through which passengers or baggage pass. 'at any place' restricts nothing.

Places borrowed from LVMC 11.60.010, quoted in d8: 'every such bus stop, bus stand, taxicab stand, other stand or origin or destination point shall be designated by appropriate signs'. A bus stop is st.transit_stop ('a bus stop, bench, shelter or platform for public transport passengers') or st.curb_zone kind bus_stop ('a signed or marked length of curb'); a bus stand (DEF-NRS-484A-035) and an origin or destination point, designated by signs, are the signed bus zone, st.curb_zone kind bus_stop; a passenger loading zone is st.curb_zone kind passenger_loading. rel.occupies anchors the bus at the place where it halts.

Nearest carriers only (atom gap): st.curb_zone kind bus_stop and st.transit_stop say a place serves buses, never which route's origin or destination point it is; no atom ties a bus to its assigned route.

Nearest carriers only (atom gap): ru.emergency_vehicle is a class ('Not a stand-in for: a responding emergency vehicle'), not a peril the bus's halt answers to; sig.hazard is 'both indicators flashing together', a signal, not the emergency. No atom carries an emergency.

compositions.quote: every such bus stop, bus stand, taxicab stand, other stand or origin or destination point shall be designated by appropriate signs

applicability: The subject is a bus and not a tour bus, its footprint overlaps a street (st.highway, rel.occupies), it does not occupy a bus stop, signed bus stand, passenger loading zone (st.transit_stop; st.curb_zone of kind bus_stop or passenger_loading) or the signed origin or destination point of its assigned route (atom gap of span d7), and no emergency is under way (atom gap of span d9).
obligation: It is not the case that the subject is at rest (drv.motion.complete_halt with p.halt_speed_tolerance) with a door open (sig.door_open), unless the halt is behind another road user ahead of it in the same lane within p.queue_halt_gap (rel.ahead_behind_in_lane, rel.surface_gap), or at a travel region it occupies governed by a traffic signal, stop sign, yield sign or railway signal or gate, or under a person's stop direction (dev.governs, dev.human_direction).

The purpose of loading or unloading passengers or baggage is read through the halted bus having a door open; a halt with every door closed is not a halt for that purpose.

A bus stand and an origin or destination point designated under LVMC 11.60.010 are read through the signed bus zone on the road (st.curb_zone kind bus_stop), the signs being the evidence of the designation.

segmentation.text: The operator of a bus,
other than a tour bus,
shall: Enter a bus stop, bus stand, passenger loading zone or origin or destination point
on a public street
in such a manner that the bus when stopped to load or unload passengers or baggage
shall be in a position with the right-hand front wheel of such vehicle not farther than eighteen inches from the curb
and the bus approximately parallel to the curb so as not to unduly impede the movement of other vehicular traffic.

elements.justification: 'bus' is admitted as DEF-NRS-484A-030::bus; ru.aggregate is 'membership of a legal aggregate'; 'the operator of' is a relational role, never membership.
'tour bus' is admitted as DEF-LVMC-11-02-150::tour_bus; ru.aggregate is 'membership of a legal aggregate'.

The places the bus enters: a bus stop is st.transit_stop ('a bus stop, bench, shelter or platform for public transport passengers') or st.curb_zone kind bus_stop ('a signed or marked length of curb'); a bus stand ('a fixed area in or adjacent to the highway to be occupied exclusively by buses', DEF-NRS-484A-035) and an origin or destination point are posted bus places, the signed bus zone, st.curb_zone kind bus_stop; a passenger loading zone is st.curb_zone kind passenger_loading. 'Enter' places the bus in it: rel.occupies anchors the bus to the zone it stands in.

'street' applies DEF-NRS-484A-265 'the entire width between the boundary lines of every highway inside the territorial limits of a city when any part of such highway is open to the use of the public', which 'public' repeats; st.highway is 'the entire public way between its boundary lines', not the roadway alone. rel.occupies anchors the bus on it.

'when stopped' is the state of rest: drv.motion.complete_halt, 'at rest at the observation — "complete cessation from movement"' (DEF-NRS-484A-255). 'to load or unload passengers or baggage' is a purpose, read by the conduct it explains: a door open (sig.door_open, 'a door open; side in {traffic, curb}') through which passengers or baggage pass.

The curb is st.road_edge, 'curb or edge of the roadway'. Its distance from the bus is st.region_geometry, 'the ground distance from a road user's body outline to it (zero when they overlap)', compared with the stated eighteen inches; 'Not a stand-in for: occupancy' does not apply, a distance is read. That the curb is on the bus's right-hand side is prim.region_lateral_offset, 'the signed lateral offset (m, left positive) of a structure region from a road user': negative for a curb on the right. Same anchoring as the index's 'or at the curb' (st.region_geometry, st.road_edge).

operationalizations.standard: approximately parallel to the curb so as not to unduly impede the movement of other vehicular traffic
operationalizations.convention: the bus counts as approximately parallel to the curb, and so not projecting across the adjacent travel lane, where the absolute cosine between its heading (kin.heading) and the designated direction (st.lane_direction) of a travel region it occupies (rel.occupies, st.travel_region), whose carriers run along the curb, is at least p.curb_parallel_cos, the bus-stop alignment tolerance of transit stop design guidance

applicability: The subject is a bus and not a tour bus; at the observation it is at rest (drv.motion.complete_halt with p.halt_speed_tolerance) with a door open (sig.door_open), and its footprint overlaps a bus stop, bus stand, passenger loading zone or origin or destination point (st.transit_stop; st.curb_zone of kind bus_stop or passenger_loading) on a street (st.highway).
obligation: Some road edge lies on the subject's right (prim.region_lateral_offset negative) at a ground distance from the subject's body outline (st.region_geometry) of at most the stated eighteen inches; and for some travel region the subject occupies, the absolute cosine between the subject's heading and that region's designated direction is at least p.curb_parallel_cos.

narrowings.why: 'The operator of a bus' is read through the bus's own controlled motion, whoever or whatever is at the controls.
A bus stand and an origin or destination point are read through the posted bus zone on the road (st.curb_zone kind bus_stop), the posting being the evidence of their designation.
The purpose of loading or unloading passengers or baggage is read through the halted bus having a door open.

The right-hand front wheel is read through the bus's body outline: the wheel lies within the outline at its right side, so the body's ground distance to the curb on the right, with the bus parallel to the curb, is the wheel's distance less the tyre's small inset from the body side; a wheel's own position is not in the vocabulary. A bus whose body is within the stated distance but whose wheel is beyond it by less than that inset is read as compliant.

'so as not to unduly impede the movement of other vehicular traffic' is read only through the bus's alignment with the curb (and its curb distance in c6): the movement of actual other traffic is not read.
